newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss government committee examines Scientology.
newsitem.headline: Swiss government committee examines Scientology.

text.p: The Swiss government has a group of experts looking into the activities of the Church of Scientology, a spokesman for the Swiss justice ministry said on Tuesday.
The investigation into the U.S.-based group, which has offshoots in many countries, is being conducted by a subcommittee formed by the ministry's consultative commission for state security.
"The task of this subcommittee is to investigate whether Scientology has any impact on the internal security of Switzerland," Viktor Schlumpf, Justice Department spokesman said.
He said the work of the subcommittee would be concluded in the coming months. It was uncertain whether there would be any report published after it finished its work, he said.
Gabriela Arm, lawyer for the Church of Scientology in Zurich, said the organisation has about 5,000 members in Switzerland.
She did not expect the subcommittee to find any reasons why scientology should pose a threat to Swiss national security.
She said it was also protected under Swiss law applying to religious freedom.
The issue of whether Scientology is a religion or not has been subject to controversy in some European countries.
Germany does not recognise it as an official religion, a decision which has drawn fire from Scientologists.
